answer: Latency-triangulated presence stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer posts a $35 bond and opens a challenge port. Second, five random verifiers ping it and triangulate its location from round-trip times, so two agents on one rack cannot both pass. Third, the check repeats weekly; a moved or cloned machine burns the bond and bans the key ninety days. Fourth, job limits rise only after thirty days of distinct presence. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 machines in 1,000 places plus $35,000, all lost when caught. Like dawn light on a reef, each lantern must hang in its own place.
